record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let X be a smooth contractible algebraic surface, properly embedded in C^N, and for large R let X_R={φ<R^2} be the resulting bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain in X, where φ(x)=||x||^2. If X is not isomorphic to C^2, must X_R fail to be biholomorphic to any bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain in C^2?

evidence.quote: QUESTION. Assume that X as above is not isomorphic to C2. Is it true that then XR is not biholomorphic to a bounded (strictly) pseudoconvex d omain in C2 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth contractible complex algebraic surface that admits a proper closed algebraic embedding into some $\mathbb{C}^N$. Define $\varphi : X \to \mathbb{R}$ by $\varphi(x) = \|x\|^2$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the standard Euclidean norm on $\mathbb{C}^N$. For all sufficiently large $R > 0$, the sublevel set
$$X_R = \{x \in X : \varphi(x) < R^2\}$$
is a relatively compact, strictly pseudoconvex domain in $X$ with smooth boundary. Assume that $X$ is not biholomorphic (equivalently, not isomorphic as an algebraic variety) to $\mathbb{C}^2$. Prove or disprove: for every such $R$, the domain $X_R$ fails to be biholomorphic to any bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^2$.
artifact.category_tag: contractible algebraic surfaces and pseudoconvex domains
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific question concerning whether bounded strictly pseudoconvex sublevel sets of properly embedded smooth contractible algebraic surfaces (other than $\mathbb{C}^2$) can fail to be biholomorphic to bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$. Related works on contractible/exotic affine surfaces and on uniformization of Kähler surfaces appear, but none directly settle the stated problem. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Smooth contractible hypersurfaces in C^n and exotic algebraic structures on C^3
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of smooth contractible algebraic hypersurfaces and exotic algebraic structures, related context for contractible surfaces and their embeddings.
status_evidence.claim: Related work exists on contractible algebraic surfaces/hypersurfaces but does not directly resolve the pseudoconvex biholomorphism question.

status_evidence.title: On homology planes and contractible 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses contractible algebraic surfaces (homology planes) including Ramanujam-type and Zaidenberg-type surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background on contractible algebraic surfaces but does not settle the biholomorphism question for pseudoconvex sublevel sets.
